conviction_note: Findings sum to +0.4: the strongest item is an inference from CNA's own filings that the ~$1.20 bar sits at Q2's run rate, and Q2 carried a $77M after-tax corporate mass-tort charge that Q3 has not historically carried. Against it sit peer proxies on workers' comp and catastrophe losses. Because CNA bought only -1.1% and +2.1% on its last two ~14-20% beats, p_up is held at 54 on an abs move of 2.6, so the scaled number (+0.21) is about half the findings sum. The beat read (+8% vs bar) is much stronger than the reaction read.
bar: Core EPS about $1.20 for Q3 2026 from two analysts: ChartRow $1.19 (https://chartrow.com/quote/cna/earnings), Earnings Whispers $1.20 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/CNA), Chartmill $1.23 (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CNA/estimates). Two sources agree to within a cent and the spread is 4c, so the bar is treated as sourced but thin. The prior-year quarter was $1.50 core (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21175/000002117525000093/q32025exhibit991.htm). There is no company EPS guide; the company guided Q3 fixed-income and other NII to ~$575M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021175/000002117526000043/q22026ex994earningsremarks.htm).
positioning_check: FINRA short interest (via equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/cna/short-interest): 3,988,584 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 9.03 days to cover, up from 2.88M on 2026-07-31 and 3.82M on 2026-09-30. That is 1.47% of 270.6M shares outstanding. Loews owns about 90-92% (sweep row; https://www.panabee.com/news/loews-earnings-q1-2026-report), so the true float is about 22M shares and short interest is roughly 15-18% of float: a crowded and rising short. The options chain is unusable (ATM spread 196% of mid, 532 contracts of open interest), so there is no skew; the put/call OI ratio is 2.64 on a trivial base. The stock is +5.6% over 20 days, +1.1% over 5 days and -11.5% from its 52-week high.

findings.finding: On CNA's own numbers, the ~$1.20 consensus for Q3 2026 sits at Q2 2026's $1.19 core EPS. Q2 included a $77M after-tax Corporate charge for legacy mass tort, and Q2 2025 had an $88M one. In Q3 2025 the Corporate core loss was only $25M and core EPS was $1.50. Seasonally, Q3 has no such charge, so stripping out about $50M of Corporate drag alone is worth about +$0.18/share against a bar set at Q2's level.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Core EPS beats have been damped. Q3 2025 printed $1.50 against a $1.25-1.46 consensus and the stock moved -1.12% (baseline 2025-11-03). Q2 2026 printed $1.19 against $1.04 (+14%) for +2.13% (2026-08-03). The Q1 2026 miss ($0.83 against ~$1.26), with adverse development, cost -7.95% (2026-05-04).
findings.why_not_priced: With only two analysts, the bar looks like Q2 rolled forward. If it already allowed for Q3's lighter Corporate seasonality, consensus would sit nearer $1.35-1.40 than $1.19-1.23. The stock is 11.5% below its high and a rising short is leaning against it.
findings.independence: The Q3 2025 Corporate core loss of $25M comes from a different document, the Q3 2025 release (https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/ca/news/breaking-news/cna-financial-reports-record-core-income-in-q3-555258.aspx). The bar comes from the aggregators cited under bar. This is inference, not a company statement: analysts may already model adverse P&C development (as in Q1) in place of the Corporate charge.

findings.finding: CNA guided Q3 2026 fixed-income and other net investment income to about $575M, up from $570M in Q2, and full-year 2026 to about $2.3B (+2%). Total Q2 NII was $701M (+6% year on year). Limited-partnership and equity income is the swing item.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Higher fixed-income NII was cited as a driver of the Q3 2025 beat, which sold off -1.12%. NII has not moved this stock alone.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, because it sits inside company guidance. The residual is LP/equity income, which follows market returns with a lag.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1. Travelers reported record Q3 NII of $1.098B, +6% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000086312/000008631226000180/a991pressrelease93026.htm).

findings.finding: Peer workers'-comp deterioration. Hartford's Middle & Large Business underlying combined ratio rose to 99.5 in Q3 2026 from 91.4 a year earlier (91.3 in Q1, 95.3 in Q2), driven mainly by a higher workers'-comp loss ratio. NCCI puts the industry's 2025 accident-year workers'-comp combined ratio at 102 against 91 calendar-year, with releases bridging the gap. CNA's Commercial segment (middle market and national accounts) writes workers' comp with rates down low single digits, and Q2 favorable development came partly from workers' comp. Commercial's underlying ratio was already 92.8 against 90.6.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Underlying deterioration plus adverse development drove the Q1 2026 print to -7.95%. Q2's 2.5-point underlying deterioration came with a beat and the stock rose +2.13%.
findings.why_not_priced: Hartford reported on 2026-10-27, after CNA last spoke, and CNA has no call to absorb it. If the market had priced a read-across to CNA's Commercial workers' comp, CNA would have lagged into the print; instead it is +5.6% over 20 days.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not CNA's own number. NCCI AY 2025 combined ratio of 102: https://riskandinsurance.com/workers-compensation-remains-profitable-as-premium-dips-and-severity-climbs/. Against it, Hartford's own Business Insurance favorable development still came primarily from workers' comp ($61M; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000874766/000087476626000079/ex991earningsnewsrelease93.htm), so the deterioration is current-year and not yet in reserves. Workers' comp is only part of CNA Commercial, which is about 40% of P&C.

findings.finding: Peer catastrophe losses rose year on year in Q3 2026, mainly from US severe convective storms. Travelers was at $538M against $302M, Chubb at $705M against $285M and W.R. Berkley at $85.9M against $78.5M; Hartford fell to $106M from $389M. Gallagher Re puts US SCS insured losses at $43B or more through Q3, alongside Hawaii hurricane impacts. CNA's Q3 2025 cat load was low at 1.5 points of combined ratio, so a year-on-year headwind is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Lower cats helped the Q3 2025 beat, which still went -1.12%. Cats were 3.6 points in Q1 2026 (-7.95%, though reserves led that move) and 2.3 points in Q2 2026 (+2.13%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The peer prints are public and analysts set cat loads, but a 2-analyst bar is rarely updated for peer cat data.
findings.independence: Gallagher Re 9M26 report (https://www.artemis.bm/news/gallagher-re-estimates-global-insured-cat-losses-at-92bn-for-9m26-lowest-since-2019/) puts global 9M losses at their lowest since 2019, which cuts against a large cat hit. Hartford's lower Q3 cats point the other way. Net, this is a small proxy.

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 peer reserve tone in commercial lines was benign. Travelers' Business Insurance had $41M of favorable prior-year development from 'better than expected loss experience in all major product lines' (excluding a $295M asbestos addition), against $125M unfavorable in Q3 2025. Selective had no net unfavorable development, against 3.7 points adverse a year earlier. Cincinnati Financial released $94M. Adverse development in excess casualty and professional lines is what sank CNA's Q1 2026 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior-year development is the line this stock has punished: Q1 2026 had 4.1 points of adverse development and fell -7.95%. Q2 2026 had zero P&C development and rose +2.13%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had extrapolated CNA's Q1 adverse-development risk forward, the stock would not have recovered +5.6% in 20 days. The rally suggests it has partly read the benign peer tone already. Remaining value: the 2-analyst bar may still embed adverse development.
findings.independence: Selective 10-Q Q3 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000230557/000023055726000027/sigi-20260930.htm. Cincinnati: https://finviz.com/news/408038/cincinnati-financial-reports-third-quarter-2026-results. Against it, Travelers shares fell ~4.4% on their own beat (https://finviz.com/news/403588/travelers-shares-fall-44-despite-third-quarter-earnings-and-revenue-beating-estimates), so the sector has sold beats. Peer favorability also does not confirm CNA's specific weak lines (professional E&O, excess casualty). Sized for that.

findings.finding: Q3 is when CNA runs its annual Life & Group reserve review (long-term care morbidity, cost-of-care inflation and structured settlements). Last year it cost $7M pretax for LTC and $2M for structured settlements, essentially neutral, with statutory LTC margin at $1.5B. Q2 2026 Life & Group swung to a $10M core loss from $1M of income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two reviews (2024: $15M pretax, 2025: $7M) were immaterial and did not visibly move the stock (Q3 2025: -1.12%).
findings.why_not_priced: Neither analyst can model it; it is a fat-tailed event that has run near zero. Last year morbidity was revised unfavorably, so the left tail is real.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 remarks say Life & Group benefits were 'generally in line with expectations' and that assumption updates come in Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021175/000002117526000043/q22026ex994earningsremarks.htm). That points toward near-neutral.

findings.finding: CNA's own underlying trend is deteriorating. The P&C underlying combined ratio was 94.5 in Q1 2026 and 94.2 in Q2, against 92.1 and 91.7 a year earlier, and Q3 2025's comparable was 91.3. P&C rate was flat in Q2 and International rate was -5%. The Q3 print will show about 3 points of year-on-year underlying deterioration and core income well below last year's record $1.50.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 carried a 2.5-point underlying deterioration yet beat, and rose +2.13%. Q1 2026 deteriorated 2.4 points with a miss and fell -7.95%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are public company numbers and the bar is $0.30 below last year. The residual is optics, because a headline falling year on year against the Q3 2025 record may draw sell-side caution.
findings.independence: Same document as findings 1 and 2. Q1 2026 figures: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000021175/000002117526000029/q12026exhibit991.htm.

findings.finding: A crowded, rising short in a tiny float. Short interest is 3.99M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (9.0 days to cover), up from 2.88M on 2026-07-31. With Loews holding about 90-92% of 270.6M shares, that is roughly 15-18% of the free float.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. The largest move in the baseline (-7.95%) came on a miss; upside reactions have been +2.13% to +4.03%.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregators quote short interest as 1.1-1.5% of shares outstanding, not of float, so the crowding is invisible on screens. On a beat, 9 days to cover in a ~355k-share daily tape is a squeeze mechanism.
findings.independence: Massive gives 3.82M and 5.0 days at 2026-09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/cna). The ~92% Loews stake is from an aggregator (https://www.panabee.com/news/loews-earnings-q1-2026-report) and ~90% per the sweep row. The rising short may itself reflect informed bearishness on the underlying trend (finding 7).

outside_window.finding: CNA plans its asbestos and environmental pollution reserve review for Q4 2026. It will be reported with Q4 results in February 2027, though Q3 remarks may preview it.

searched_and_found_nothing: CNA company news October 2026: only the earnings-date announcement (https://finviz.com/news/401924/cna-financial-to-report-third-quarter-2026-results-on-november-2)
Loews buy-in of the CNA minority, or 2026 CNA rating changes: nothing found
A large Q3 2026 casualty reserve charge at a major peer: none found (Selective, Travelers and Cincinnati were favorable or neutral)
A standalone Q3 2026 PCS cat estimate: none, only Gallagher Re's 9M figure
Options skew: the chain is unusable (baseline)
Loews reports Q3 on the same morning, so it carries no information before the print

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew and an unusable chain. The +5.6% 20-day run-up and the rising short pull opposite ways, and my mildly positive lean sides with the run-up and against the shorts, so p_up is held near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a fact is not a reaction): the Corporate-seasonality beat finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6, because the last two 14-20% beats moved -1.1% and +2.1%.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller than company number): Hartford/NCCI workers' comp cut from -0.5 to -0.4 and peer cats from -0.3 to -0.2. Both stay filed and labelled as proxies.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): peer reserve tone cut from +0.4 to +0.3, because Travelers sold off on its own beat and peer favorability does not cover CNA's weak lines.
Lesson 7 (positioning): the crowded short counts once, as the positioning finding, cut from +0.4 to +0.3 because the rising short may be informed. It was not also used to shrink the negatives.

Lesson 6 (bar): three estimate sources agree within 4c ($1.19/$1.20/$1.23), so findings are not capped further. The A&E review is moved to outside_window. The own-trend finding is cut from -0.3 to -0.2 because its numbers are public company figures already inside the bar.
